questions.question: An Ethernet hub receives a signal on one port. Where is the signal repeated?

options.A: Only on a port in a matching IP prefix
options.B: Only on the port learned for the destination
options.C: Only on a designated gateway port

questions.explanation: A hub is a multiport repeater and has no MAC forwarding table.

questions.question: Which behavior is permitted by matching full-duplex Ethernet endpoints?

options.A: Alternating transmission under a shared collision domain
options.B: Transmission only after a collision backoff
options.D: Transmission only when the opposite endpoint is powered off

questions.explanation: A full-duplex point-to-point link permits both directions simultaneously.

questions.question: Four workstations attach to one half-duplex Ethernet hub. How many shared collision domains do they occupy?
questions.explanation: The hub repeats signals across its ports, so the stations share one collision domain.

questions.question: What does a half-duplex Ethernet station do after detecting a collision?

options.A: Changes its IP address and retries
options.B: Stops the attempt and waits a backoff before retrying
options.C: Starts a TCP retransmission immediately at the MAC layer
options.D: Continues sending the original frame uninterrupted

questions.explanation: CSMA/CD uses collision handling and a randomized backoff to retry medium access.

questions.question: A hub is replaced by a switch with a full-duplex link to each capable host. What changes for Ethernet contention?

options.A: All hosts still contend for the hub's collision domain
options.C: The hosts no longer contend for one shared half-duplex medium
options.D: The switch must run CSMA/CD between all ports

questions.explanation: Each host gets a dedicated full-duplex link, removing shared-medium collisions.

questions.question: Two old hubs connect to separate switch ports in half duplex. How many collision domains do those hubs and their attached stations create?
questions.explanation: The switch separates contention on the two hub-facing segments.

questions.question: One end of a legacy link is forced to full duplex and the other reports half duplex. Under simultaneous traffic, which fault should be investigated first?
questions.explanation: The half-duplex end follows collision rules while the full-duplex end transmits independently.

questions.question: An illustrative switch output reports half duplex and increasing late collisions. Which pair of physical-layer checks is most relevant?

options.A: Gateway distance and DHCP lease duration
options.B: Peer subnet mask and DNS server
options.C: Remote ARP cache and TCP window
options.D: Peer duplex and excessive segment length

questions.explanation: Duplex mismatch and excessive propagation delay can produce late collisions.

questions.question: An interface now operates in full duplex. Why should an engineer compare collision counter readings over time before diagnosing a fault?

options.A: Collisions and IPv4 discards share a required counter
options.B: A single snapshot identifies the peer duplex exactly
options.C: Existing counters can predate the current mode
options.D: Full duplex adds one collision per receive frame

questions.explanation: Historical counts alone do not show the fault is currently occurring.

questions.question: A switch port connects to a hub while a separate port connects to a workstation. Which statement describes their duplex settings?

options.A: The workstation must use the same duplex as every hub station
options.B: The hub-facing link uses half duplex and the independent workstation link can use full duplex
options.C: Both links must use full duplex because the switch supports it
options.D: The switch must use half duplex on both ports

questions.explanation: Duplex is set or negotiated per link. A shared hub requires half-duplex Ethernet.
